# Screen protocol

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_docs.py -- do not edit. Run `make generate` after changing its source. -->

How a viewer and a SimMirror server talk over the screen socket: a hello each way, then frames and events out and a whitelist of input in. The schemas in [`protocol/v1`](../../protocol/v1/) are the one definition -- the Python and TypeScript types are generated from them -- and [`protocol/README.md`](../../protocol/README.md) walks through a socket's life and the rules for changing the protocol.

## Close codes

| Code | Constant | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `1014` | `CLOSE_BAD_GATEWAY` | The device's connector stopped answering while the socket was open. |
| `4400` | `CLOSE_BAD_MESSAGE` | The client's first message was not a hello, or was not JSON. |
| `4401` | `CLOSE_UNAUTHORIZED` | No ticket, or a ticket that was already used, has expired, or was made for another scope. |
| `4403` | `CLOSE_FORBIDDEN` | The simulator is off for this scope, or the Host or Origin is not allowed. The close reason says which. |
| `4406` | `CLOSE_UNSUPPORTED` | The client's protocol version is not supported, or none of the encodings it decodes is offered. |
| `4410` | `CLOSE_STOPPED` | The device was stopped. There is nothing to reconnect to. |
| `4412` | `CLOSE_RESTARTING` | The device is restarting and will be back. Reconnect. |
